newsitem.title: USA: MGM Q2 meets forecasts despite events of Tyson fight.
newsitem.headline: MGM Q2 meets forecasts despite events of Tyson fight.

text.p: MGM Grand Inc., owner of the MGM Grand hotel and casino in Las Vegas, Thursday reported second quarter earnings in line with forecasts despite a loss of revenue after last month's Mike Tyson, Evander Holyfield prize fight there.

Following the June 28 championship bout, in which Tyson was disqualified for biting Holyfield's ears, casino operations were disrupted in a scramble to get out of the arena, and the casino was closed for one and one-half hours.
Typically prize fights bring in hordes of gamblers and the casinos count on them to help spur revenues and earnings.
Thursday, MGM Grand reported second quarter net income of $33 million, or 56 cents a share, versus $20.6 million, or 41 cents a share, in the second quarter one year ago.
Financial analysts had expected the company to earn 56 cents a share in the second quarter, according to investment research firm, First Call.
Revenues were up at $209 million, less promotional expenses, as compared with $189 million last year.
"We're feeling pretty good about the fact that our company really doesn't depend on one specific fighter or one specific event," President Alex Yemenidjian said in a teleconference.
He also noted MGM Grand faced a tough comparison to last year's second quarter because the casino played particularly lucky in 1996, and the month of June was relatively slow throughout Las Vegas.
"In the midst of all those circumstances, we have $33 million of profit which is an all time record for our company," he added.
MGM Grand shares were up $6.25 at $34.81 on the New York Stock Exchange following its second quarter earnings report.

Following the Tyson/Holyfield fight, MGM Grand gave notice to boxing promoter Don King that it wants to terminate the agreement to hold six Tyson bouts in the hotel's arena. The latest Holyfield fight was the fifth match under that arrangement. Tyson was recently banned from boxing in Nevada, but can re-apply after one year.
Yemenidjian said the company currently has no agreements to hold boxing matches with any other fighter or promoter.

Meanwhile, the company has scheduled other events, such as concerts by the Rolling Stones and Bee Gees, and hopes its new conference centre will bring in casino business when it opens next year. The centre already has $100 million worth of advance bookings.

Plans to expand the MGM Grand remain on track as does its proposal to build a casino in Detroit. The company is continuing to pursue the land it needs to build a hotel and casino in Atlantic City and pursuing gambling licenses for overseas expansion in South Africa.
